concepts.en: How can we care for our environment?

summary.big_en: A habitat is the place where a living thing lives.

glossary.def: Look for what is the same and what is different.
glossary.example: Compare two habitats near your school (p.5).

glossary.def: The place where a living thing lives.
glossary.example: A wall can be a habitat for a small plant (p.3).

glossary.def: A word you write on a drawing to name a part.
glossary.example: Label your drawing to say what each thing is (p.4).

glossary.def: A small copy of a real thing.
glossary.example: Make a model of a habitat for fish in a box (p.5).

glossary.def: The air, water and land around us.
glossary.example: People, animals and plants all live in the environment (p.2).

glossary.def: The place where a living thing stays.
glossary.example: The wall is the plant's home (p.3).

glossary.def: Near the place where you live.
glossary.example: Your local environment has many habitats (p.4).

points.t: A habitat gives a living thing everything it needs to live (p.3).
A habitat can be very small, like a wall, or very large, like a forest (p.3).
Plants cannot move from place to place, but animals can move in their habitat (p.4).

glossary.def: A thin line where something is split open.
glossary.example: Roots grow down a crack to find soil (p.8).

glossary.def: Say what something is like.
glossary.example: Describe the place a plant lives (p.7).

glossary.def: A place that is very hot and very dry.
glossary.example: A cactus can live in a hot desert (p.11).

glossary.def: A picture you take with a camera.
glossary.example: Take a photograph of your plant (p.8).

glossary.def: Act as if you are someone or something else.
glossary.example: Pretend you are one of the three plants (p.10).

glossary.def: Write or draw what you see.
glossary.example: Record your plants and their habitats in a table (p.8).

points.t: All plants need water, and many plants grow in or by water (p.7).
Rice needs a warm habitat with a lot of light and water (p.10).
A cactus needs a very hot habitat with light and very little water (p.11).
Pond weed needs a habitat underwater, and it must not get very cold (p.11).

summary.big_en: Animals often hide, so we look for clues to find them.

glossary.def: Make something want to come.
glossary.example: More insects may attract other animals (p.17).

glossary.def: Small signs that show an animal was here.
glossary.example: Tracks and droppings are clues (p.14).

glossary.def: The waste an animal leaves behind.
glossary.example: Droppings tell us that an animal is near (p.14).

glossary.def: Something an animal lays, with a baby inside.
glossary.example: Insects lay eggs in the sticks (p.17).

glossary.def: Go somewhere you cannot be seen.
glossary.example: Snails like to hide in cool damp places (p.16).

glossary.def: A very small animal, like a beetle or an ant.
glossary.example: An insect hotel is a habitat for insects (p.17).

glossary.def: Make an animal afraid so it runs away.
glossary.example: Be quiet so that you don't scare the animals (p.15).

glossary.def: Marks that an animal's feet leave on the ground.
glossary.example: We can see tracks in soft soil (p.14).

points.t: Animals hide from us, so they are harder to observe than plants (p.15).
Clues that an animal lives here are tracks, droppings, eaten leaves and birds singing (p.14).
Small animals need a safe place to live close to food (p.17).

summary.big_en: We dig up rocks to build things, but digging damages the environment.

glossary.def: Take water in.
glossary.example: Chalk absorbs water (p.23).

glossary.def: Something that breaks rock into pieces with a bang.
glossary.example: Sometimes we use explosives to break rock (p.24).

glossary.def: Small stones from a river bed.
glossary.example: From rivers we dig sand, gravel and pebbles (p.25).

glossary.def: A place where we dig rock deep underground.
glossary.example: We get coal and salt from a deep mine (p.24).

glossary.def: A place where we dig rock at the surface.
glossary.example: We get limestone and slate from a quarry (p.24).

glossary.def: A small piece you take to look at.
glossary.example: Sofia and Zara have a sample of rock (p.22).

glossary.def: Another name for small rocks.
glossary.example: Stones is another name for small rocks (p.25).

glossary.def: Move water round and round.
glossary.example: Add water and swirl the water (p.26).

glossary.def: Water cannot go in.
glossary.example: Slate is waterproof, so we use it for roofs (p.21).

points.t: Planet Earth is made of rocks (p.20).
Rocks can be strong, soft or waterproof, and we choose a rock for the job (p.21).
Most rocks do not burn, but coal is a rock that burns (p.21).
When people dig up rocks, plants and animals lose their homes (p.25).

summary.big_en: We can care for the environment by picking up litter and recycling.

glossary.def: Rubbish left in the wrong place.
glossary.example: This beach is covered in litter (p.28).

glossary.def: What a thing is made of.
glossary.example: The arrows tell us that the material can be used again (p.30).

glossary.def: A place kept safe for plants and animals.
glossary.example: The children want to make the garden into a nature reserve (p.30).

glossary.def: Dirty air, water or land.
glossary.example: Pollution is bad for animals and plants (p.28).

glossary.def: Keep something safe.
glossary.example: We can protect the animals and plants on the beach (p.28).

glossary.def: Use a material again instead of throwing it away.
glossary.example: We can recycle glass, paper, plastic, card and metal (p.30).

points.t: Pollution harms the animals and plants that live near it (p.28).
The recycling sign has arrows that mean the material can be used again (p.30).
A nature reserve makes a better habitat for plants and animals (p.30).
Litter can be dangerous, so talk to an adult before you pick it up (p.31).

quiz.stem_en: What is a habitat?

choices.en: The place a living thing lives

quiz.why_en: A habitat is the place where a living thing lives (p.3).

quiz.stem_en: What does a habitat give a living thing?
quiz.why_en: A habitat gives the living thing everything it needs to live (p.3).

quiz.stem_en: Which one can move around its habitat?
quiz.why_en: Animals can move in their habitat, but plants cannot (p.4).

quiz.stem_en: Is the eagle's habitat large or small?
quiz.why_en: The eagle's habitat is around forests and lakes, so it is very large (p.3).

quiz.stem_en: What does every plant need?
quiz.why_en: All plants need water (p.7).

quiz.stem_en: Where does a cactus live?
quiz.why_en: A cactus needs a habitat which is very hot and needs very little water (p.11).

quiz.stem_en: What does rice need a lot of?
quiz.why_en: Rice needs a habitat which is warm, with lots of light and water (p.10).

quiz.stem_en: Where does pond weed live?
quiz.why_en: Pond weed needs a habitat underwater in a pond, lake or river (p.11).

quiz.stem_en: Why are animals harder to observe than plants?
quiz.why_en: Animals may hide from us, so they are harder to observe (p.15).

quiz.stem_en: Which one is a clue that an animal was here?
quiz.why_en: Tracks, droppings and eaten leaves are clues (p.14).

quiz.stem_en: Where do snails like to hide?
quiz.why_en: Snails like to hide in cool damp places (p.16).

quiz.stem_en: What is an insect hotel made from?
quiz.why_en: The insect hotel is made from sticks and stems (p.17).

quiz.stem_en: What is planet Earth made of?
quiz.why_en: Planet Earth is made of rocks (p.20).

quiz.stem_en: Why do we use slate for roofs?
quiz.why_en: Slate is waterproof (p.21).

quiz.stem_en: Which rock burns?
quiz.why_en: Most rocks do not burn, but coal is a rock that burns (p.21).

quiz.stem_en: Where do we dig rock deep underground?
quiz.why_en: A deep mine is a place where we dig up rock deep underground (p.24).

quiz.stem_en: What happens when people dig up rocks?
quiz.why_en: When people dig up rocks they damage the environment: plants and animals lose their homes (p.25).

quiz.stem_en: What is litter?

choices.en: Rubbish left in the wrong place

quiz.why_en: Litter is rubbish left where it should not be (p.28).

quiz.stem_en: Which of these can we recycle?
quiz.why_en: We can recycle glass, paper, plastic, card, metal and electrical cells (p.30).

quiz.stem_en: What do the arrows on the recycling sign mean?

choices.en: The material can be used again

quiz.why_en: The arrows tell us that the material can be used again (p.30).

quiz.stem_en: What should you do before you pick up litter?
quiz.why_en: Litter can be dangerous, so talk to an adult before you pick up litter (p.31).
